correctness.rationale: For connected complete multipartite K_{n1,...,nr} and f∈{−1,1,2}^V, every vertex in part i has open-neighborhood sum W−s_i, so total signed neighborhood condition is iff W−s_i>=1 for all parts. Every minus-one vertex in i sees a label 2 iff C−c_i>=1, needed only when a_i>0. Counting each feasible part count triple by product n_i!/(a_i!b_i!c_i!) proves the full weight enumerator with no duplicate functions. Summing all r inequalities yields (r−1)W>=r; integer W therefore >=2 for all r>=2, so no negative powers. Independent direct vertex-adjacency and part-count feasibility agreed for every nondecreasing multipartite profile with total 2..6; in particular K_{2,2} polynomial is 4x²+9x⁴+8x⁵+6x⁶+4x⁷+x⁸. This is all graph sizes, not inferred from finite tests.

originality.rationale: The source Koster–Volkmann–Wehrmann 2026 concerns signed total Roman domination and domatic minima for complete multipartite graphs; abstract-accessible material does not state all-function weight enumerator, but full text was unavailable (Oxford VPN disconnected), a substantial residual risk for an intermediate part-count lemma. Related full published Resultary result on signed Roman domination uses CLOSED neighborhoods W−s_i+μ_i>=1, unlike required OPEN W−s_i>=1; the complete multipartite total Roman enumerator instead labels {0,1,2} and imposes no-isolated-positive rather than −1 open sum. These closely related formulas neither equal nor algebraically imply this exact STRD distribution merely by relabeling. An especially similar exact partwise profile suggests methodology is elementary; novelty is narrow to the signed-total all-weights enumeration.

value.rationale: The signed total Roman domination number is only the minimum exponent; the exact polynomial counts all feasible signed-total functions at each weight on an arbitrary connected complete multipartite profile. That natural enumerative invariant is useful for multiplicities, distributional comparisons and extremizer counts and is not supplied by scalar domination/domatic numbers. Although the proof is a short transparent specialization of partwise neighborhoods and related variants exist, the exact all-weights invariant is mathematically motivated; no general theorem beyond this complete natural family is claimed.

limitations: r>=2 connected complete multipartite only, single signed total Roman functions not domatic families.
